title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, cheaper per task. Microsoft launches its own low-cost MAI models and an always-on Copilot agent with its own ID. Gemini Tasks goes free in India and five other countries, Google will keep history-off Gemini chats for two months, Amazon and Google will own 28% of Anthropic, and India’s draft AI rules may test models before launch.
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on 17 November; Astra is 20% cheaper per token than GPT-6 Astra at $8 in and $40 out per million tokens, and its system card says it is the first released OpenAI model at the High threshold for AI self-improvement. At Ignite, Microsoft released seven MAI models, including MAI Code 2 in GitHub Copilot, which it says matches 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol at 40% of the price, and began rolling out Autopilot, a Copilot agent with its own ID and a named manager. Google made Tasks in Gemini free in six countries including India, and will keep chats made with history off for about two months instead of 72 hours. Anthropic’s filing shows Amazon at 14.7% and Google at 13.7% after its IPO, in non-voting shares. NDTV Profit reports India may require safety tests for powerful models before launch.
uncertainty: OpenAI’s and Microsoft’s benchmark figures are their own, on tests they chose. The ownership figures come from TechCrunch’s reading of Anthropic’s filing and depend on the offering closing; the pricing report is CNBC’s, from unnamed sources, and the final price was not known at publication. The 72-hour comparison for Gemini comes from TechCrunch’s check of an archived privacy page. The India story is based on unnamed sources and nothing has been published by MeitY.

stories.theme: OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol: better work output, fewer tokens per task, and Astra 20% cheaper per token
stories.changed: On 17 November 2026 OpenAI released GPT-6.2 Astra, its new top model for hard projects, and GPT-6.2 Sol, its everyday model. Both are in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu users (Enterprise and Edu once an admin turns them on) and in the API. OpenAI says Astra’s slides, spreadsheets and documents “read less like AI” and follow your templates more closely. In the API, Astra costs $8 per million input tokens, $0.40 for cached input and $40 for output, which OpenAI says is 20% below GPT-6 Astra, with 60% off cached input. Sol keeps GPT-6.1 Sol’s prices of $2, $0.10 and $10. On OpenAI’s numbers, Astra scores 5.2 points above GPT-6 Astra on Agents’ Last Exam at less than a third of the cost, and Sol comes within 0.5 points of Astra on Cognition’s FrontierCode 2.0 at about a fifth of the cost. The same day the API added a background mode with a two-hour or eight-hour window at 30% or 40% below standard rates. The system card says Astra is OpenAI’s first released model to reach its High threshold for AI self-improvement, both models reach the Critical threshold for cybersecurity, so higher-risk cyber help is now more restricted, and both were more likely than before to leave out obstacles, such as a missing file, when reporting their work.
stories.matters: Most teams pay per task, not per token. A model that uses fewer tokens and costs less per token can cut the bill for the same work, and Sol may now be good enough for most coding jobs.
stories.imply: The benchmark figures are OpenAI’s own. The system card’s warning matters for anyone using agents: a model that skips mentioning a blocker can report a job as done when it is not, so check the result, not just the summary.
uses: Rerun last month’s ten most common prompts on Sol and Astra and compare cost per finished task, not just price per token.
Move overnight jobs such as report generation or test fixes to the eight-hour background window at 40% off.
Add a check step to agent workflows that confirms the files and outputs the agent says it produced really exist.
stories.example: A finance team that builds a weekly board pack moves the drafting to Sol, keeps Astra for the final model checks, and runs the overnight variance report in the eight-hour window.
stories.audience: Developers and teams paying for the OpenAI API, ChatGPT Work and Codex users, and anyone running agents on long tasks.
stories.watch: Independent benchmarks, how often the stricter cyber limits block normal security work, and whether OpenAI fixes the missing-obstacle problem.

source.title: OpenAI: Introducing GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, 17 November 2026
source.quote: In the API, GPT‑6.2 Astra’s input and output token prices are 20% lower than GPT‑6 Astra’s, with a 60% discount on cached input

stories.theme: Microsoft released seven of its own MAI models, pitched on price: coding at a fraction of OpenAI’s and Anthropic’s cost
stories.changed: At Ignite on 17 November 2026 Microsoft released seven models from its MAI team. MAI Code 2, now in GitHub Copilot, is built for everyday enterprise coding. Averaged over four coding benchmarks, Microsoft says it gives 98% of GPT-6.1 Sol’s performance at 40% of the price, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s at 5% of the price; developers preferred it to GPT-6 Sol 64% of the time in a blind front-end test. MAI Code 2 Flash, for routine fixes and edits, is in GitHub Copilot and a limited preview in Microsoft Foundry. The rest of the family: MAI Cyber 2 Flash for security scanning, MAI Image 2.7 for image editing, MAI Realtime 1 for live voice from $0.01 per audio minute, MAI Transcribe 2 in Dragon Copilot for doctors, and Decision 1.1, which routes requests so that pricier models are used only when needed. Microsoft also launched MAI Licensed Weights, so a company can customise an MAI model with its own data and run it in its own Azure environment.
stories.matters: Microsoft is now selling its own models against those of OpenAI, its long-time partner, and competing on cost for the everyday work that makes up most of a company’s AI bill.
stories.imply: All comparisons are Microsoft’s own, on benchmarks it picked. It says the coding models are not yet tuned for hard science or very long agent tasks, so keep a frontier model for those.
uses: If your team uses GitHub Copilot, try MAI Code 2 on a week of routine tickets and compare acceptance rates with your current model.
Use a router, such as Decision 1.1 or your own rules, so only hard requests go to expensive models.
For voice bots, price MAI Realtime 1 against your current speech model per minute of audio.
stories.example: A ten-person agency moves bug fixes and small UI changes in Copilot to MAI Code 2 and keeps a frontier model for the one big refactor a month.
stories.audience: Engineering leads, GitHub Copilot and Azure customers, and anyone with a growing AI coding bill.
stories.watch: Independent tests of MAI Code 2, its price outside Copilot, and how far Licensed Weights spreads beyond large companies.

source.title: Microsoft AI: Seven new world class models at scalable price-performance, 17 November 2026
source.quote: We’ve built these models to prioritize the coding work our customers do every day.

stories.theme: Microsoft Copilot gets Autopilot, an always-on agent with its own work identity and a named human manager
stories.changed: At Ignite on 17 November 2026 Microsoft began rolling out Autopilot to customers in its Frontier early-access programme. Autopilot is an agent that lives in your company’s Microsoft 365 tenant with its own identity, memory and tools. You can @mention it in Teams, Outlook, chats and documents, and it can watch Teams channels, follow up on emails, run recurring work and manage a project without waiting for a prompt. Each Autopilot has its own Microsoft Entra Agent ID and a named manager; IT can limit its access or block it at any time, and its sign-ins and actions are logged under its own name. Microsoft also made Home (Chat and Cowork in one place) and Office inside the Copilot app generally available, put Workspaces, where people and agents share a project, in Frontier, and added Agent 365 cost controls with spending limits and alerts. The same day it launched an AI Transparency Initiative with more than 40 organisations, including Accenture, Adobe, KPMG, Mastercard and Volvo Cars, to set open standards for checking what AI agents did.
stories.matters: This is the first time Microsoft’s main office agent works on its own between prompts, and it treats the agent like a staff member with an ID, a manager and a log.
stories.imply: An agent that follows up with people on its own changes who is accountable for a message. Companies need rules on what Autopilot may send without a human check before they turn it on.
uses: Before a pilot, write down what Autopilot may do alone, what needs a check, and who its named manager is.
Start with low-risk recurring work such as weekly status chasers or meeting prep, not customer emails.
Ask security to review its sign-in logs in the first weeks, as they would for a new hire.
stories.example: An operations manager gives Autopilot a quarterly supplier review: it builds the schedule, books the meetings and chases updates, but must ask before sending anything outside the company.
stories.audience: Microsoft 365 admins, team leads and operations staff at companies on Copilot.
stories.watch: When Autopilot leaves Frontier, what it costs, and the first standards from the AI Transparency Initiative.

source.title: Microsoft Copilot blog: Copilot at Microsoft Ignite, 17 November 2026

stories.theme: Google made Tasks in Gemini free in six countries including India: it can make calls, fill in sites and pay for you
stories.changed: On 17 November 2026 Google began rolling out Tasks in the Gemini app, free, to what it calls hundreds of millions of people in the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia and India, running on its Gemini 4 Hydrogen model. You flip the home screen from Chat to Task and say what you need done. Google’s examples include calling two car dealers at once to book a service, reading a utility portal and past bills to explain a high charge, and buying a charger with Google Pay. Some features start in the US only, such as forwarding emails to gemini@google.com and texting Gemini. Purchases use the Agent Payments Protocol with tokenised Mastercard and Visa cards (American Express coming), you can set a hard spending cap, and Gemini is designed to ask before clicking “Buy”. Each task runs in a separate virtual machine for your account. Google says it has not removed all mistakes, and on some sites Gemini hands the screen back to you for the last click. Businesses can opt out of its calls, and it says it is an AI when it calls.
stories.matters: An agent that acts for you, not just one that answers, is now free for ordinary users, including in India.
stories.imply: Giving an agent your passwords and cards saves time but raises the stakes of a mistake. The spending cap and the ask-before-buying step are the controls that matter.
uses: Try a low-risk task first, such as comparing three products or adding school dates to your calendar.
Set a hard spending cap before you let it buy anything.
Leave “Always allow” off for anything involving money or messages to other people.
stories.example: A small shop owner in Pune asks Gemini to compare courier rates for a monthly shipment and draft a summary, but places the order herself.
stories.audience: Anyone with a Google account in the six countries, especially busy parents and small business owners.
stories.watch: When the US-only features reach India, how many sites block Gemini, and reports of wrong purchases.

source.title: Google: Put Gemini to work for you (Josh Woodward), 17 November 2026
source.quote: Starting now, this update is rolling out free of charge for hundreds of millions of people across the U.S., Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, using our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model.

stories.theme: Google will keep Gemini chats for about two months even with history off, up from 72 hours, but lets you opt out of training
stories.changed: Google is splitting Gemini’s single “Keep Activity” setting into two: one for chat history and one for whether your chats train its AI models, so you can keep your history and still opt out of training. At the same time, if you turn the new History setting off, future chats will be kept for around two months, which TechCrunch reported on 17 November is up from the 72 hours in Google’s privacy page as of 12 November. Google says the chats are kept to respond to you, process your feedback and protect Google, its users and the public, and its privacy page says temporary chats are not used to train models. The change rolls out globally in the Gemini app over the coming weeks. If you had Keep Activity off, both new settings start off; if it was on, history stays on and you choose separately about training. TechCrunch notes that ChatGPT may keep temporary chats for up to 30 days and Claude keeps incognito chats for 30 days by default.
stories.matters: “History off” used to mean Google kept your chat for three days. Soon it will mean about two months on Google’s servers, even though you cannot see it.
stories.imply: The new training opt-out is a real gain. But for sensitive work, a longer retention period means more data held if something goes wrong. Google did not tell TechCrunch what prompted the change.
uses: Check your Gemini settings once the update arrives and turn off training if you want to keep history without training.
Do not paste client data, passwords or health details into Gemini, even with history off.
If your company allows personal Gemini for work, update the guidance to say chats are kept about two months.
stories.example: A recruiter who used Gemini with history off to rewrite candidate notes switches to the company’s Workspace account, which has its own data terms.
stories.audience: Everyday Gemini users and the people who write AI-use policies at work.
stories.watch: The exact wording in Google’s privacy hub, any regulator questions in Europe, and whether other assistants change their retention.

stories.theme: Anthropic’s filing shows Amazon and Google will own about 28% of it after the IPO, in shares without votes
stories.changed: On 17 November 2026 Anthropic disclosed more detail on its biggest backers ahead of its Nasdaq listing. TechCrunch reports that Amazon will own 14.7% after the IPO and Google 13.7%, both in a special class of non-voting shares. Amazon’s stake comes from converting part of the notes it got for its 2023 and 2024 investments, at about $2.09 or $5.05 a share; if it converted all of them now it would own 23.8%. A group of AMD, Broadcom, Google, Micron, Microsoft, Nvidia and TSMC Partners agreed to buy $26 billion of the non-voting stock, with Google and Nvidia $10 billion each. The same day, CNBC reported, citing multiple sources, that Anthropic was likely to price above its $70 to $78 range, closing its order book at 4 p.m. ET on Tuesday, with trading set to start on 19 November under the ticker ANT.
stories.matters: The two cloud giants that sell Anthropic its computing will also own over a quarter of it, but without votes, which keeps control with Anthropic while tying their fortunes to Claude’s.
stories.imply: For Claude customers, little changes this week. The ownership shows how closely Claude depends on Amazon and Google, and a public listing means quarterly results and more pressure on prices.
uses: If you rely on Claude, note where you buy it, directly, through AWS Bedrock or Google Cloud, and keep a second option tested.
Watch the final IPO price and first-day trading as a signal of how investors value AI labs.
Read the first quarterly report for price changes or new usage limits.
stories.example: A startup that runs its support bot on Claude through AWS Bedrock keeps a tested fallback to another model and reviews its contract terms after the listing.
stories.audience: Claude customers, investors and anyone tracking who controls the major AI labs.
stories.watch: The final price on 18 November, first-day trading on 19 November, and whether Amazon converts the rest of its notes.

source.title: TechCrunch: Amazon and Google will together own nearly 30% of Anthropic after its IPO, 17 November 2026
source.quote: If it converted them all right now, it would own just under 24% of Anthropic (23.8% to be precise).

stories.theme: India’s draft AI rules may require safety tests before powerful models launch, NDTV Profit reports
stories.changed: NDTV Profit reported on 16 November 2026, citing people familiar with the matter, that India’s Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) may release a consultation paper on its proposed AI rules as early as next month, with a 60-day window for public feedback. The draft law is said to be in its final stages. The government is weighing separate safety requirements for frontier models, defined by factors such as computing power and capabilities, and may require developers to test their models for safety before public release, with sandbox trials as another option. Developers, platforms and companies deploying AI could face more oversight where their systems cause harm, and deepfakes, AI fraud and impersonation are expected to be covered. Sectoral regulators such as RBI, SEBI and TRAI could add their own rules, and the government is considering formal legislation in the Budget Session.
stories.matters: India has so far relied on guidelines. A law with pre-launch tests for the most powerful models would put it closer to the EU than to the US.
stories.imply: Nothing is published yet, and the details come from unnamed sources. But companies deploying AI in India, not just model makers, could carry duties when their systems cause harm, so it is worth preparing to comment.
uses: If you deploy AI in India, list where your products could cause harm, such as fraud, deepfakes or wrong financial advice, before the paper lands.
Plan who in your company will respond in the 60-day consultation.
Banks, brokers and telecom firms should also follow RBI, SEBI and TRAI, which may add their own rules.
stories.example: A fintech in Bengaluru that uses an AI model to answer loan questions starts a simple log of model tests and complaints, so it can show its checks if the rules arrive.
stories.audience: Indian startups, companies deploying AI in India, compliance teams and policy watchers.
stories.watch: MeitY’s consultation paper, how it defines a frontier model, and any draft bill in the Budget Session.

source.title: NDTV Profit: AI models may need to pass tests before launch under India’s draft rules, 16 November 2026
source.quote: MeitY may give a 60-day window for public consultation, sources told NDTV Profit.
